findings.location: architecture.md Impact for steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs; Reuse NAV_PROBE (feature_nav_collapse.rs:1246); Boundaries Driven ports
findings.obligation: Dependency direction must be unambiguous: Boundaries state no step module depends on another step module, and D14 places the shared head reader in support/ for that reason; the S2 lane must obey the same direction.
findings.observation: S2 Impact says the new step module feature_nav_icon_rail.rs reuses the nav probe reading rather than declaring a second one, and Reuse marks NAV_PROBE (feature_nav_collapse.rs:1246) Extend. NAV_PROBE is a private const (grep: uses only at feature_nav_collapse.rs:1246 and :1300), so the new module can reach it only by a step-to-step import or a visibility change, contradicting the stated invariant. The design names neither a move into support/ nor an explicit exception.
findings.remediation: Decide the owner: move NAV_PROBE and its reading into support/ and have both step modules call it, or record the step-to-step dependency as a deliberate exception in Boundaries naming the visibility change. State the verified direction in the S2 agreement.

findings.location: architecture.md D14 and request finding 3; ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-002 Consequences
findings.obligation: The user decided all five findings are fixed (K12); finding 3 names the xtask head_scripts copy as one of the duplicates. Narrowing user-fixed scope needs recorded user confirmation, and the claim that the gate copy and the oracle copies can contradict each other needs an observation that they agree today.
findings.observation: D14 is a DECISION, not CONFIRMED, and keeps the xtask copy separate; no recorded user confirmation of that narrowing exists in K10-K14. No law or architectural test pairs xtask head_script_tags (check_arch.rs:1935) with the shared acceptance reader on the shipped head, so the independent-second-implementation claim is asserted but its agreement is unobserved.
findings.remediation: Record the user confirmation (or an explicit reduction with provenance) that finding 3 is met by one shared owner for the acceptance copies plus a deliberately separate gate copy; add an observation or test that both readers give the same verdict on the shipped head and on staged shapes.

findings.location: architecture.md D16, Failures B1/B5, ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-002 Consequences, design/head_guard.qnt
findings.obligation: Each failure direction of the widened membership test needs an explicit state, refusal message and discriminating observation.
findings.observation: Only the false-negative direction (identifiers built at runtime, B5) is stated. The reverse is not: membership is by names alone, so a legitimately deferred asset naming localStorage/sessionStorage and documentElement for settled-DOM work (keyboard.js and board-dnd.js already name documentElement; a storage name flips them) is classed a stamper and refused with advice to remove defer, putting a non-pre-paint script on the render-blocking path. B1 says the asset reads the stored choice and stamps, which the names test does not establish. head_guard.qnt equates recognition with names, so it cannot show this case.
findings.remediation: Add the false-positive failure (state, refusal wording saying the gate decided by names and how to resolve it) to Failures and Risks; add a staged shape for a deferred asset naming both to the L6 generator or S1 oracle; align B1 and ADR wording with what the test establishes.

findings.obligation: A MECHANICAL review question whose tool was not executed is incomplete by construction; the recorded Quint/Apalache claims and mutant kills must be replayable from a scratch copy.
findings.observation: Replay failed with No space left on device creating a scratch directory in the VM; the receipt is unreplayed by this review. Model hashes match, but per-property falsification and kills are unverified here.
findings.remediation: Free space in the shared local-dev VM, then replay the receipt argv (verify gateMatchesPaint and classifierSeesEveryStamper; run init_defer_attr_narrow and init_hide_none kills) from a fresh directory, record results, and re-review.

findings.location: architecture.md B1 and S1 public oracle (b)/(c) versus (f) and B10; ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-003 Decision (1)-(2)
findings.obligation: Each gate refusal must give one coherent remedy: the gate decides by names alone, so one input class (names storage and documentElement, tag carries defer) yields one entry, and the oracle must not require contradictory wording for it.
findings.observation: The aliased true stamper in (b)/(c) and the settled-DOM neighbour in (f) have the same source-visible shape, so the gate emits the same entry for both. B1 and (b)/(c) require that entry to tell the contributor to remove the attribute; B10 and (f) require it to warn that dropping defer puts a non-pre-paint script on the render-blocking path. The design never says the entry carries both messages or how it reconciles them, so as written an implementation passes one oracle case only by failing the other or by emitting self-contradictory advice.
findings.remediation: Specify one refusal wording for the names-plus-deferring-attribute shape that distinguishes the two cases for the contributor (if this asset really stamps before paint, remove the attribute; if it only touches the settled DOM, split the read or record an exception, never drop defer), and restate B1, (b)/(c) and (f) to assert that single text's required clauses.

observations.text: Round-2 finding resolved: ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-004 (Accepted) gives the names-only shape one refusal text with five clauses C1-C5; architecture.md D24, the (b)/(c)/(f) expectation (line 2447) and the failure list (line 2451) say the same, and the oracle asserts the aliased-stamper and settled-DOM entries are the SAME text. The contradiction between two remedies for one input class is gone.

Supersession chain consistent: ADR-003 status is Superseded by 004; the ADR list names 004 Accepted; no remaining text in brief.md or architecture.md says the only remedy is to remove the attribute or drop defer. The wrong remedy is stated as accepted-but-unobserved with guards (C5 plus the standing plain-head-script review obligation), not as a proven property; no DESIGNED_NOT_BUILT claim is promoted to observed.

Evidence gap, not blocking: design/head_guard.qnt judge() still holds the pre-004 message for the refuse shape ('reads stored state and stamps documentElement ... drop defer, async and type=module') at lines 46-48. ADR-004 says the models are unchanged because the correction was to specified text, not a checked property. True for the checked properties (verdict, not message text), but the qnt string is not the C1-C5 text and claims stamping; the authority for the text is architecture.md D24 and acceptance, so no implementer is misled if they follow those.

diagnostic: Round 3: ADR-NAV-ICON-RAIL-004 resolves the round-2 finding and introduces no new defect. One non-blocking evidence gap recorded: the qnt model message string for the refuse shape predates the five-clause text; message text is not a checked property.
